   109	Response to this Notice
   110	Enclosed as part of this Notice is a document entitled Response Options for Pipeline Operators in
   111	Enforcement Proceedings. Please refer to this document and note the response options. All
   112	material you submit in response to this enforcement action may be made publicly available. If you
   113	believe that any portion of your responsive material qualifies for confidential treatment under 5
   114	U.S.C. § 552(b), along with the complete original document you must provide a second copy of
   115	the document with the portions you believe qualify for confidential treatment redacted and an
   116	explanation of why you believe the redacted information qualifies for confidential treatment under
   117	5 U.S.C. § 552(b).
   118	Following your receipt of this Notice, you have 30 days to respond as described in the enclosed
   119	Response Options. If you do not respond within 30 days of receipt of this Notice, this constitutes
   120	a waiver of your right to contest the allegations in this Notice and authorizes the Associate
   121	Administrator for Pipeline Safety to find facts as alleged in this Notice without further notice to
   122	you and to issue a Final Order. If you are responding to this Notice, we propose that you submit
   123	your correspondence to my office within 30 days from receipt of this Notice. The Region Director
   124	may extend the period for responding upon a written request timely submitted demonstrating good
   125	cause for an extension.

   156	PROPOSED COMPLIANCE ORDER
   157	Pursuant to 49 United States Code § 60118, the Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety
   158	Administration (PHMSA) proposes to issue to City of Richmond (City) a Compliance Order
   159	incorporating the following remedial requirements to ensure the compliance of the City with the
   160	pipeline safety regulations:
   161	A.
   162	
   163	In regard to Item 1 of the Notice pertaining to the failure to follow procedures
   164	during installation of a 12-inch expansion coupling, the City must, within 90 days
   165	of receipt of the Final Order, develop and implement a training program focused on
   166	special fittings such as Dresser Style. City gas utility construction and maintenance
   167	personnel shall be trained with the updated content and requalified for the covered
   168	task.
   169	
   170	B.

170	B.
   171	
   172	In regard to Item 2 of the Notice pertaining to the failure to ensure training of
   173	covered tasks provided necessary knowledge and skills, the City must update its
   174	Operator Qualification training program to specifically include training on the
   175	installation of restraining and non-restraining expansion couplings, including
   176	special fittings such as Dresser Style 63 and provide the updated training program
   177	to the Director, Eastern Region, within 90 days of receipt of the Final Order.
   178	
   179	C.
   180	
   181	It is requested (not mandated) that City of Richmond maintain documentation of
   182	the safety improvement costs associated with fulfilling this Compliance Order and
   183	submit the total to Robert Burrough, Director, Eastern Region, Pipeline and
   184	Hazardous Materials Safety Administration. It is requested that these costs be
   185	reported in two categories: 1) total cost associated with preparation/revision of
   186	plans, procedures, studies and analyses, and 2) total cost associated with
   187	replacements, additions and other changes to pipeline infrastructure.
